key_insight: A physics-driven multiscale reduced basis built from local Helmholtz wave responses can accurately capture high-frequency wave propagation while preserving stability through a spectral coarse-to-fine construction.
engineering_relevance: This enables much smaller global systems for high-frequency wave simulation, making large-scale acoustics/elastic-wave style computations more tractable for homogeneous and strongly heterogeneous media.
method: Solve local Helmholtz problems on oversampled patches with boundary excitations to generate physically informed snapshots.
Use local generalized eigenvalue problems to select dominant modes and assemble a sparse global reduced system.
Prove multiscale stability via an inf-sup argument tied to fine-grid resolution, oversampling, and omitted local eigenvalues.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments showing accurate wavefields with substantial reductions in global dimension and solution cost, including cases with PML truncation.
watch_item: Accuracy and stability depend on adequate fine-grid resolution, oversampling depth, and retaining enough local eigenmodes; under-resolved patches or aggressive truncation may degrade performance.
paper_title: A Physics-Driven Multiscale Method for High-Frequency Helmholtz Equations
